extracted.intended_audience: NLP / AI researchers and practitioners working on evaluation of creative writing and LLM-generated narratives
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and using a standardized benchmark and dataset (LitBench) to reliably evaluate automated judges and reward models for creative writing by measuring agreement with human preferences, training on human-labeled preference pairs, and validating on novel LLM-generated stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement with human preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate automated judges by their agreement with human preferences (e.g., Claude-3.7-Sonnet reached 73% agreement with human preferences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher percentage agreement with human preference judgments is used as the primary reliability signal for automated evaluators; report model-vs-human agreement numbers on held-out comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debiased, human-labeled story comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Use debiased, human-labeled story comparisons as the core annotation format (the LitBench held-out test set comprises 2,480 debiased, human-labeled story comparisons drawn from Reddit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debiasing of pairwise comparisons is necessary to avoid spurious signals; ensure annotation process mitigates contextual or position biases when collecting preference labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Held-out test set for evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess models on a held-out test set (LitBench provides a held-out test set of 2,480 pairs) rather than training data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a held-out, debiased test split to measure generalization and to benchmark zero-shot judges and trained reward models fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large training corpus of human preference labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Train evaluation/reward models using a sizable corpus of human preference pairs (LitBench includes a 43,827-pair training corpus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger, high-quality human-labeled corpora enable training of reward models that can surpass off-the-shelf judges; report training-set size and provenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark zero-shot off-the-shelf LLM judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Include benchmarking of off-the-shelf (zero-shot) LLM judges to establish baselines (the paper benchmarks zero-shot LLM judges and identifies the strongest OTS judge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare multiple OTS models in zero-shot settings to understand current baseline reliability before training specialized reward models; report per-model agreement scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train and evaluate reward models (Bradley-Terry and generative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Train Bradley-Terry and generative reward models on human preference data; both model types achieved 78% accuracy in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train both pairwise-ranking models (e.g., Bradley-Terry) and generative reward models, evaluate their accuracy against human-labeled held-out pairs, and compare to OTS judges to demonstrate improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate model rankings with online human study on novel LLM-generated stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct an online human study to validate that reward model rankings align with human preferences on newly LLM-generated stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation on novel, out-of-training LLM-generated content is required to demonstrate that reward models generalize and meaningfully reflect human judgments beyond the benchmark dataset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard accuracy/agreement metrics for reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report accuracy and agreement metrics (e.g., percent agreement with human preferences) as quantitative measures of evaluator performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear quantitative metrics (accuracy, agreement rates) for comparability across models and judges; include confidence intervals or statistical tests where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release dataset and models for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Release LitBench and trained reward models to provide a vetted resource for reliable, automated evaluation and optimization of creative writing systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public release of benchmark data and trained evaluators enables reproducible comparisons and community adoption; include documentation on debiasing and annotation procedures.
